stemMd: Which quantity is conserved when a chemical equation is correctly balanced?

options.label: A
options.textMd: The number of substances listed on each side

options.label: B
options.textMd: The mass of each individual molecule

options.label: C
options.textMd: The number of atoms of each element

options.label: D
options.textMd: The number of gas molecules only

options.label: E
options.textMd: The total number of molecules in every reaction

explanationMd: Ordinary chemical reactions rearrange atoms without creating or destroying them. A balanced equation therefore has equal counts of every element on both sides. Total molecule count can change even though atoms and total mass are conserved.

distractorRationale.e: Molecule counts can change, as in two molecules combining into one.
distractorRationale.d: Gas molecule counts need not be conserved.
distractorRationale.b: Different products have different molecular masses.
distractorRationale.a: A reaction can have different numbers of reactants and products.
